Hi Rodney,

On Mon, 19 May 2003 10:47:08 -0700, Rodney Siegel wrote:

> >Distance samplers,

> >I want to run an analysis in Distance 4 in which I estimate a detection
> >function for a relatively frequently detected 'surrogate' species, and then
> >apply that detection function to a rarer species which likely has a similar
> >detectability function (based on similar vocalizations, behavior,
> >etc.). What's the best way to set this up? I should add that I want to
> >fit a global detection function for the surrogate species (because I have
> >no reason to think detectability should vary across the study site), but I
> >need stratum-specific density estimates for the rare species (because
> >density surely varies across the site). My first idea was to use the data
> >filter to combine data for the surrogate species and the rare species, and
> >then to post-stratify on species name... but this precludes producing
> >density estimates specific to the real strata-- which are defined
> >geographically.

> >Thanks for any help anyone can provide!

> >******************************************
> >Rodney Siegel
> >The Institute for Bird Populations
> >P.O. Box 1346
> >Point Reyes Station, CA 94956-1346
> >tel:(415) 663-2051
> >fax:(415) 663-9482
> >email: rsi...@birdpop.org
> >web: www.birdpop.org

In any case, I guess I'm best placed to answer your question, but I'm forwarding
my reply to the list as it's quite a common question.

Look in the online help, under Multipliers in the Index. At the bottom of that
page, under "Additional uses of multipliers" it shows you how to do exactly what
you want, which is to use a multiplier to specify the probability of detection
for the rarer species, basing the probability on that estimated from the common
species. The only downside of this approach is that you can't then use the
bootstrap to estimate variance for the rarer species, as the multiplier SE is
not used during the bootstrap (see online help Appendix - Program Reference,
Model Definition Properties, Multipliers). A minor inconvenience though.

Cheers,

- Len

Hmmm - sneaky! Great idea Jeff.

This will include both the surrogate and rarer species in the detection function
estimation, where the multiplier approach I suggested could use only the surrogate
species or both species, depending on how you specify data selection in the
detection function analysis.

The big advantage of Jeff's approach is that you can do the whole thing in one
analysis, rather than the two that mine would take.

You could also have a go at bootstrap variance estimation with Jeff's approach,
but the results wouldn't be strictly correct as you'd want to resample by transect
and when a transect is picked that should include the transect from the "surrogate
species stratum" and that same transect in the "rarer species strata". (You could
do slightly better by having the original strata with area 0 for surrogate
species, and repeating the strata with true area for the rare species -- at least
you'll be resampling transects within strata then, even if the transects for
surrogate and rare species are still not matched.) I shouldn't think it'll create
a huge bias in variance estimate in practice however, especially since variance of
f(0) estimate is usually a small component of variance in D.

- Len
